# Boron One boosts Serbia project economics in updated study

[Frederic Tomesco](/external-author?external_author=Frederic Tomesco) | October 14, 2026 | 2:10 pm  [News](https://www.mining.com/category/news/) [Canada](https://www.mining.com/region/canada/) [Europe](https://www.mining.com/region/europe/) [Specialty Minerals](https://www.mining.com/commodity/specialty-minerals/)

![](https://www.mining.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/core_storage-piskanja.jpg)

A view of the core storage area at Piskanja. Credit: Boron One Holdings.

Canadian explorer Boron One Holdings (TSXV: BONE) has outlined a higher projected return, annual revenue and after-tax net present value (NPV) for its Piskanja boron project in Serbia.

An updated preliminary economic assessment (PEA) [released Wednesday](https://www.juniorminingnetwork.com/junior-miner-news/press-releases/1256-tsx-venture/bone/212878-boron-one-holdings-inc-announces-positive-preliminary-economic-assessment-pea-for-its-piskanja-boron-project.html) forecasts an after-tax internal rate of return of 89%, compared with 79% in the 2022 study. At a 10% discount rate, the NPV rises about 6% to $558.8 million from $524.9 million, while average annual gross revenue increases to $140.4 million from $126 million.

Initial capital costs remain unchanged at $79.9 million, with payback projected within a year of starting commercial production. However, the proposed mine life falls to 13 years from 16, while average annual earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization drop to $87.7 million from $91.3 million.

The economic assessment excludes inferred resources. The study remains preliminary, and the resources don’t have demonstrated economic viability.

“Given these and other factors, future activities are justified to continue to advance project development,” Boron One said in Wednesday’s statement. A future work program will be discussed to define the necessary steps toward a feasibility study and the eventual construction of an underground mine, it added.

## High-tech applications

Boron is considered a critical mineral in the United States, the United Kingdom and the European Union, but not in Canada. Its compounds are used in fertilizers, specialty glass, ceramics, fibreglass insulation, as well as electrolyte additives in some electric-vehicle batteries.
